questions.question: No open backlog item covers this work. Should the two PRs sit under a new item (which then needs a trace)?

options.label: One item, BK-415 (Recommended)
options.description: One BK-415 covers the research record and the RFC-0020 experiment. The trace is shared, opens in PR 1 and continues in PR 2. The item stays open until run B decides.

options.label: Two items, BK-415 + BK-416
options.description: One for the research record, which closes with PR 1, and one for the RFC and run B. That means two traces and two index entries.

options.label: No item
options.description: Research and the Draft RFC go in without an item or trace. Run B is then tracked nowhere in the backlog.

questions.question: Should the BK-366 annotation go into PR 1? It says the rise in bug share starts in July 2026, before /ship.

options.label: Yes, dossier note in PR 1 (Recommended)
options.description: I re-run shipera.py and add a dated note to the BK-366 dossier with the derivation, linking to report.md. The BACKLOG.md line stays as it is.

options.label: Report only
options.description: The finding stays in report.md. BK-366 is left untouched for the later decision batch.

options.label: Neither
options.description: The bug-share figure stays out of both PRs.

questions.question: Should the /ship variant for run B be built in PR 2 or in a later PR?

options.label: Later PR (Recommended)
options.description: PR 2 is the Draft RFC only, so it touches no .claude/skills/ files and can merge while run A is still active. The variant is built after you approve the RFC's Phase 0.

options.label: In PR 2
options.description: The RFC and the variant skill ship together. PR 2 then can't merge until run A finishes, because it changes .claude/skills/.

questions.question: Run B will be watched with tokkit.py, and the report's BUG-280 section comes from it. Where should it live?

options.label: Research folder (Recommended)
options.description: Port it, parametrised, into sdd/research/token-usage/ next to the analysis scripts. The RFC names it as run B's instrument. It is not a hatch target and gets no tests.

options.label: scripts/ + hatch target
options.description: Make it real tooling: scripts/, a hatch entry, a Drift-gate docstring and tests. This makes PR 1 noticeably larger.

options.label: Leave in tmp/
options.description: Don't commit it. The report cites its output only, and run B depends on an uncommitted tool.

questions.question: BK-415 has to sit under a backlog promise. None of the existing ones fits cleanly: § 7 is about the CI/local gate's wait, and § 8 is about lookup by key. Where should it go?

options.label: New § 9 (Recommended)
options.description: New section '9. A delivery costs only what it needs'. Promise: a session's token spend follows the work it does, not the context it has piled up. Review rounds, orient and gate waits are measured before the process changes. Later token items get a home here.

options.label: Re-argue § 8
options.description: Widen § 8's promise from 'reads what it needs' to cover a session's carried context as a whole. BK-414 and BK-415 then share it.

options.label: Under § 7
options.description: File it under 'The gate costs only what it needs'. That fits the gate-robustness part only, not the review loop.

options.label: Agent work is efficient here (Recommended)
options.description: '## 9. Agent work is efficient here'. Promise: an agent session spends its tokens on the work, not on context it has piled up or rounds that repair its own fixes, and a change to how sessions work is measured before it becomes process. Your wording, scoped to tokens and measurement.

options.label: A delivery costs only what it needs
options.description: '## 9. A delivery costs only what it needs'. Promise: a session's spend follows the work it does, not the context it has piled up. This mirrors § 7's 'The gate costs only what it needs'.

questions.question: The scripts that group transcripts into work items (correlate, phase, levers) need a session-ID-prefix → item mapping. Where should that mapping live?

options.label: Outside the repo, --work FILE (Recommended)
options.description: The scripts take a --work JSON naming groups by session-ID prefix. That JSON stays in tmp/, next to the extracts it needs anyway. Results record item names only, plus the input file's SHA-256, so no session ID is committed.

options.label: Committed mapping
options.description: Commit work_items.json with 8-character session prefixes per item. Nobody can rerun it without the extracts, but a reader sees which sessions were grouped.

options.description: Commit results/prose_labels.json: per finding the key (PR-round-index), class, checkable, loop_ref and target_kind. No comment text or paraphrase. The bodies stay fetchable from the public PRs with prose_fetch.py, and a reader can audit any label.

options.label: Aggregates only
options.description: Commit only the class-by-round tables. Individual labels can't be audited, and the spot-check can't be repeated.
